verses.text: It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.

verses.text: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.

verses.text: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.

verses.text: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.

verses.text: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.

verses.text: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.

verses.text: In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.

verses.text: In my futile life I have seen both of these: A righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.

verses.text: Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?

verses.text: What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?

verses.text: I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.

verses.text: And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.

verses.text: “Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.

verses.text: While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.
